The retail orders database has three tables. Each order is one customer
buying one product. `customer_id` and `product_id` in `orders` point back to
the `customers` and `products` tables.

Work out what each query returns **by hand**, using only the tables below.
Write the result as a small table. Then check your answers by running the
queries on the
[database](https://calvinw.github.io/FIT-courses/CS211/lectures/sql/create-retail-orders-brief-db.sql).

## The tables

**customers**

| customer_id | first_name | last_name |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | John | Doe |
| 2 | Jane | Smith |
| 3 | Robert | Johnson |
| 4 | Sarah | Williams |

**products**

| product_id | name | price |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Silk Blouse | 89.99 |
| 2 | Denim Jeans | 79.99 |
| 3 | Cashmere Sweater | 149.99 |
| 4 | Cotton T-Shirt | 29.99 |
| 5 | Wool Coat | 199.99 |

**orders**

| order_id | customer_id | product_id | order_date |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 | 3 | 2025-03-10 |
| 2 | 2 | 1 | 2025-03-12 |
| 3 | 3 | 4 | 2025-03-15 |
| 4 | 2 | 4 | 2025-03-18 |
| 5 | 1 | 2 | 2025-03-20 |
| 6 | 2 | 3 | 2025-03-25 |

{{< pagebreak >}}

## Level 1: one table

**1.** Products under \$100.

```sql
SELECT name, price FROM products WHERE price < 100;
```

## Level 2: joins

**6.** Each order with the customer's name and the product name.

```sql
SELECT o.order_id, c.first_name, p.name
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
JOIN products p  ON p.product_id  = o.product_id
ORDER BY o.order_id;
```

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
::: {.answer .tall}
:::
:::
::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}
\vspace{4.5cm}
:::

**7.** Who bought the Cashmere Sweater?

```sql
SELECT c.first_name, c.last_name
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
JOIN products p  ON p.product_id  = o.product_id
WHERE p.name = 'Cashmere Sweater';
```

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
::: answer
:::
:::
::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}
\vspace{3cm}
:::

**8.** Total sales across all orders.

```sql
SELECT SUM(p.price)
FROM orders o JOIN products p ON p.product_id = o.product_id;
```

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
::: answer
:::
:::
::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}
\vspace{2cm}
:::

## Level 3: GROUP BY

**9.** How much each customer spent.

```sql
SELECT c.first_name, SUM(p.price) AS total
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
JOIN products p  ON p.product_id  = o.product_id
GROUP BY c.first_name;
```

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
::: answer
:::
:::
::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}
\vspace{3.5cm}
:::

**10.** Number of orders per customer, including customers with none.

```sql
SELECT c.first_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS num_orders
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
GROUP BY c.first_name;
```

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
::: answer
:::
:::
::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}
\vspace{3.5cm}
:::

**11.** How many times each product was ordered.

```sql
SELECT p.name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS times_ordered
FROM products p
LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.product_id = p.product_id
GROUP BY p.name;
```

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
::: answer
:::
:::
::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}
\vspace{3.5cm}
:::
